scope: Installed-source audit and tiny synthetic CPU checkpoint equivalence; not production model memory, latency or clinical validation

findings.finding: low_cpu_mem_usage is explicitly popped as no longer used; adding True would be a no-op
Ordinary non-Deepspeed model construction already uses torch.device(meta)
Zip-format bin checkpoint loading already uses torch.load mmap=True
Safetensors CPU loading uses mmap-backed lazy get_slice materialization
Default up-to-four-thread eager parameter materialization is disabled by HF_DEACTIVATE_ASYNC_LOAD=1; the synchronous path returns deferred callables to avoid saturating CPU memory during conversion

verification.fixture: Complete tiny locally generated CPU float32 safetensors checkpoints; 1 layer, hidden size16, vocabulary32
assertions: Async path actually creates its materialization pool while serial path creates none
Every loaded state_dict tensor has exact key/shape/dtype and bitwise-equal bytes against both the other loader and the original synthetic checkpoint
Embedding hidden states and pooled output, or classifier logits, are bitwise equal on fixed CPU inputs
Worker overrides incoming flag0 before Torch import
No model downloads or GPU inference

limitations: Synthetic tensor/output equivalence does not measure installed full BGE checkpoint peak memory or prove clinical quality
Serial loading may not materially reduce peak memory because checkpoint loading is already mapped/lazy
The subsequent whole-model CPU half conversion and MPS transfer remain unchanged
No production-model download, GPU test or memory-threshold relaxation was performed by this audit
